HAEMATOLOGICAL EMERGENCIES IN THE ED 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
HAEMOPHILIA 
THROMBOTIC 
MICROANGIOPATHY 
• ITP 
• TTP 
• HUS 
• DIC 
SICKLE CELL CRISIS 
• Fever 
• Vaso-occlusive crisis 
• Acute chest syndrome 
• Acute splenic sequestration 
• Aplastic crisis 
• Stroke 
• Priapism 
PLEASE NOTE 
 
* High index of suspicion!!! 
* Patients may have normal vitals despite serious pathology 
* Triage in for even minor complaints & involve Haematology early 
HAEMATOLOGICAL  
EMERGENCIES 
Dr J Du Plessis / Dr R Gihwala CMJAH Emergency Department June 2020 
Contents

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Dr J Du Plessis / Dr R Gihwala CMJAH Emergency Department June 2020 
PRECIPITANTS 
*Infection 
*Dehydration 
*Hypoxia 
*Drugs (e.g. sedatives, local anaesthetics) 
*Changes in temperature 
*Trauma 
At high risk of infection due to underlying immunosuppression from: 
*Functional asplenia 
*Prophylactic treatment with hydroxyurea  
  à neutropaenia & cardiomyopathy 
TYPES OF SICKLE CELL CRISIS PRESENTATIONS 
*Fever 
-consider veno-occlusive disease, acute chest syndrome,  
 osteomyelitis, local/systemic infection 
*Vaso-occlusive crisis 
-assume this is the cause for any painful presentations 
*Acute chest syndrome 
-life-threatening lung infarction 
-assume if hypoxia + chest pain 
*Acute splenic sequestration 
-typically occurs in infants 
-associated with increased spleen size and LUQ pain 
-fall in Hb>2g/dL, thrombocytopaenia but normal or 
increased reticulocytes 
*Aplastic crisis 
-fall in Hb and reticulocytes <1% 
-triggered by Parvovirus B19 infection 
*Stroke 
*Priapism 
-stuttering (2-4 hour duration and may be recurrent) 
-severe (> 4 hours and may lead to permanent impotence) 
HAEMATOLOGICAL EMERGENCIES 
SICKLE CELL CRISIS 
ASSESSMENT 
Always consider the presence of all types of sickle cell crisis, 
regardless of the dominant presentation  
 
*Symptoms and signs of local and systemic infection 
*Respiratory signs and symptoms 
*Increasing spleen size 
*Shock and evidence of organ failure 
*Baseline and current Hb 
*CXR if fever, chest pain or hypoxia 
*CT Brain if stroke suspected  
*Consider FBC, reticulocytes, bilirubin,  
  haemolytic screen & crossmatch 
*Blood film- sickle cells & evidence of haemolysis 
https://litfl.com/sickle-cell-crisis/ 
Contents

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
HAEMATOLOGICAL EMERGENCIES 
SICKLE CELL CRISIS 
Dr J Du Plessis / Dr R Gihwala CMJAH Emergency Department June 2020 
MANAGEMENT 
RESUSCITATION 
*ABC approach 
*Correct hypoxia  
*Ensure adequate hydration – fluid bolus 20ml/kg if hypovolaemic 
*Transfuse PRCs (leuco-depleted) if Hb < 5g/dL or Hb > 20% drop from  
  baseline 
 
SPECIFIC TREATMENT 
 
*Fever 
  -empiric broad spectrum antibiotics - Augmentin® 1.2g IVI 
  -full septic workup 
*Vaso-occlusive crisis 
  -aggressive pain management à paracetamol, ±NSAIDs, opiates  
   (See pain management protocol) 
*Acute chest syndrome 
  -supplemental oxygen if hypoxic (Sats<92%) & aggressive pain  
   management à prevent hypoventi
